Complete RNA-ADT Scaling With GSE164378 3’ CITE-seq

This tutorial fits the complete scScale model to 4,000 matched GSE164378 3’ CITE-seq PBMC cells. The RNA matrix has 2,000 highly variable genes and the ADT matrix has 228 antibody features.

The main interface takes the two matched feature-by-cell count matrices and returns the full-depth fit, UMI scaling, cell-number scaling, and joint \(I(n,U)\) grid in one object.

library(scScale)
## Loading required package: Matrix
data(gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg)

X <- gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg$rna_counts
Y <- gse164378_3p_citeseq_hvg$adt_counts

dim(X)
## [1] 2000 4000
dim(Y)
## [1]  228 4000

Fit Everything

The default UMI grid is c(0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.70, 0.85, 1.00). The cell-number grid is generated automatically using absolute, log-spaced cell counts.

model <- scscale(
  X,
  Y,
  seed = 164378
)

model
## scScale joint model
##   cells: 4000
##   X features: 2000
##   X spikes: 48
##   Y dimensions: 13
##   UMI rates: 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 1
##   cell grid: 500 to 4000 (12 points)

The complete result is organized into four main components:

UMI Scaling

plot(model, type = "umi")

Cell-Number Scaling

plot(model, type = "cell")

Joint Cell-Number by UMI Scaling

Each colored line is one UMI sampling rate evaluated over the same absolute cell-number grid.

plot(model, type = "joint")

Optional Controls

The default call should be sufficient for the standard workflow. The sampled UMI depths and evaluated cell counts can still be overridden explicitly:

model_custom <- scscale(
  X,
  Y,
  umi_sampling_rates = c(0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, 1.00),
  n_grid = c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000),
  seed = 164378
)
